papers.title: ICA-S3M: switching state-space model guided automatic EEG artifact removal from independent components.
papers.summary: This paper introduces ICA-S3M, a two-stage pipeline combining independent component analysis and a switching state-space model to remove electromyographic artifacts from EEG recordings. The method significantly outperformed a CNN baseline, reducing RRMSE and improving SNR without requiring training data, and avoided the CNN's tendency to inject spurious alpha-band activity.

papers.title: Towards Personalized Edge-AI for Medicine: Efficient Neuromorphic Frameworks for Seizure Detection and Prediction
papers.summary: This preprint presents a neuromorphic framework using spiking neural networks and on-chip learning on a BrainChip Akida processor for real-time seizure detection and prediction. It achieved superior performance to state-of-the-art neural networks on several EEG datasets while drastically reducing memory footprint and energy consumption.

papers.title: Characterizing transition state in mouse vigilance with electroencephalogram-electromyogram hypnodensity.
papers.journal: Sleep advances : a journal of the Sleep Research Society
papers.summary: This study characterized vigilance-state transitions in mice using EEG/EMG recordings and manual annotations, finding distinct dynamics across transition types, with NREMS-to-REMS transitions being the longest and REMS-to-NREMS the most abrupt. SVM classifiers trained on stable-state features successfully predicted expert-defined transition midpoints.

papers.title: Meta-Analysis of Face-Validity Indicators in Automatically Detected Dog Sleep Spindles.
papers.summary: This meta-analysis evaluated automatic sleep spindle detections in dogs against three face validity criteria originally established for human EEG: spindle duration, distribution of faster spindles along the midline, and amplitude-negative chirp association. All three criteria were observed in the majority of data sets, supporting the validity of the detection method and the dog as a model for sleep spindle research.

papers.title: REM Sleep Disengagement of β Oscillations Permits Rapid Dream Movements in Parkinsonism
papers.summary: This preprint reports that in a non-human primate model of parkinsonism, pathological beta oscillations and motor impairments were attenuated during REM sleep, allowing rapid movements. Beta suppression preceded REM onset, suggesting that Parkinsonian network dysfunction is dynamically gated by brain state rather than continuously imposed.

papers.title: Single-channel gamma burst dynamics and adaptive deep learning for robust EEG motor state decoding.
papers.summary: The paper introduces a compact EEG decoding framework that models gamma burst dynamics (onset, duration, amplitude, recurrence) using an analytic wavelet transform with adaptive thresholding, combined with classical spectral features through a multi-stream adaptive deep learning model. On the WAY-EEG-GAL dataset, the approach achieved competitive performance under a single-channel constraint and improved cross-session accuracy by more than 10% over non-adaptive baselines.

papers.title: Diurnal time and sleep pressure modulate cerebrospinal fluid low-frequency oscillations in synchrony with wake-promoting nuclei
papers.summary: The study used a 34-hour sleep deprivation protocol with fMRI/EEG and NIRS to investigate how diurnal time and sleep pressure affect cerebrospinal fluid (CSF) low-frequency oscillations (LFOs). They found that CSF LFOs increase with time awake, exhibit diurnal fluctuations peaking in early morning, and are associated with vigilance and activity of the reticular activating system, but not with plasma norepinephrine or EEG slow wave activity.

papers.title: Microstates and connectivity states reveal task-related network reorganization in Alzheimer's disease patients.
papers.summary: This study compared EEG microstates and phase-based connectivity states in Alzheimer's disease (AD) patients and healthy controls before and after a memory task, with some receiving rTMS. Connectivity states were more sensitive to AD-related alterations, showing decreased task-related network stability in AD, which correlated with memory performance and amyloid-beta levels, supporting the neural efficiency hypothesis.

papers.title: Personalized, home-based transcranial alternating current stimulation for memory improvement in mild cognitive impairment: randomized, sham-controlled clinical trial protocol.
papers.summary: This paper describes a protocol for a randomized, sham-controlled, double-blind clinical trial (MemStim) evaluating personalized, home-based gamma-frequency tACS over the left angular gyrus for memory improvement in mild cognitive impairment (MCI). The trial will recruit 40 participants, use MRI-based electric field modeling for personalized montages, and measure outcomes like MoCA change and gamma-band power via hdEEG.

papers.title: An EEG-based fatigue detection framework integrating interpretable feature selection and efficient temporal modeling.
papers.summary: The paper presents AXELLSTM, an EEG-based cross-subject fatigue detection framework using nested leave-one-subject-out validation, ANOVA/XGBoost feature selection, L1-regularized channel selection, and an EfficientLSTM model with attention mechanisms. It achieved balanced accuracy of 0.7436 and Macro-F1 of 0.7143 with low computational cost, identifying frontal, frontopolar, and other channels as fatigue-relevant.

papers.title: Aftereffects of 1-week chronic intermittent hypoxia on the jaw muscle electromyographic activities during sleep in young adult rats.
papers.summary: This study exposed young adult rats to chronic intermittent hypoxia (CIH) for one week and found increased FosB expression in brainstem trigeminal premotor regions and enhanced noradrenergic fibers in the trigeminal motor nucleus, selectively increasing arousal-related digastric muscle activity during sleep without altering sleep architecture.

papers.title: Motor related potential amplitude and latency shifts with repetitive task execution as an indication of motor adaptation.
papers.summary: This study measured motor-related potentials (MRPs) during a repetitive wrist task in healthy adults and found that MRP latency and amplitude features distinguish successful from failed tasks, with longer latencies in failed tasks and three amplitude features (max, min, peak-to-peak) significantly different, suggesting MRPs reflect motor adaptation and performance.

papers.title: Respiratory phase shapes brain-heart dynamics: evidence from recurrence analysis of EEG band power and heart rate.
papers.summary: This study analyzed EEG band power and heart rate during controlled breathing in 15 healthy subjects and found that inhale-hold was associated with increased gamma power, higher recurrence rate, and elevated heart rate, while exhale-hold showed reduced gamma activity, lower recurrence, and decreased heart rate, indicating respiratory phase modulates brain-heart dynamics.

papers.title: Parent and child-reported acceptability and preference of pediatric home sleep apnea testing versus In-lab polysomnography: a pilot study.
papers.journal: Sleep advances : a journal of the Sleep Research Society
papers.summary: This pilot study compared home sleep apnea testing (HSAT) with in-lab polysomnography (PSG) in 15 children and found that HSAT was feasible and preferred by 60% of parents but only 33% of children, with frequent sensor adjustments needed, suggesting improvements in nasal cannula and pulse oximeter stability could increase acceptability.

papers.title: Capturing the multimodal dynamics of acute stress responses: Evidence from the Montreal Imaging Stress Task (MIST).
papers.journal: International journal of clinical and health psychology : IJCHP
papers.summary: This study collected multimodal data from 33 healthy young adults during the Montreal Imaging Stress Task and found that acute stress elicited coordinated changes in self-reported stress, cortisol, heart rate, pupil diameter, performance, and EEG power, with adaptive changes during the task and limited correlations between pupil and EEG changes.

papers.title: Artificial intelligence in pediatric arrhythmias: current landscape, unique challenges, and translational perspectives.
papers.summary: This review critically evaluates AI applications in pediatric arrhythmia detection and management, finding that purpose-built deep learning models show strong diagnostic performance for specific phenotypes like WPW syndrome and long QT syndrome, but most tools remain unvalidated retrospective proofs-of-concept with barriers including data scarcity and lack of prospective external validation.

papers.title: Application of a parametric supermatrix multi-task multimodal deep learning model based on electroencephalogram and peripheral physiological signal fusion in emotion recognition.
papers.summary: This study proposes a parameterized supermatrix multi-task multimodal deep learning model (PH-MTM) that fuses EEG and peripheral physiological signals for emotion recognition, achieving 95.99% and 96.51% accuracy for valence and arousal on DEAP, and 94.25% on SEED. It demonstrates improved accuracy with low computational cost, with EEG+EMG fusion performing best (99.69% and 99.74% for valence and arousal).

papers.title: Data-Driven Approaches for Autism Detection: A Comprehensive Review of Machine Learning Algorithms and Datasets.
papers.journal: International journal of developmental neuroscience : the official journal of the International Society for Developmental Neuroscience
papers.summary: This systematic review of 59 studies (2019-2025) on machine learning for autism spectrum disorder detection reports that classical ML and DL models achieve accuracies from 68% to 99% across modalities, with hybrid multimodal frameworks yielding consistent improvements (95%-99%), but highlights common flaws such as small sample sizes, demographic bias, and lack of external validation.

papers.title: Cardiac Autonomic Modulation in Seizure Disorders With and Without Interictal Epileptiform Discharges: A Retrospective Heart Rate Variability Analysis Using Archived Digital EEG Recordings.
papers.summary: This retrospective observational study compared HRV among 45 adults with seizure disorders (with or without interictal epileptiform discharges) and a non-seizure comparison group using ECG from archived EEG recordings, finding significantly lower vagally mediated HRV (pNN50, total power, HF power) in seizure patients, but no difference between the two seizure groups.

papers.title: Resting-State EEG Functional Connectivity and Independent Correlates of Cognitive Impairment in Patients with Atrial Fibrillation.
papers.summary: This study of 141 participants (63 with atrial fibrillation and cognitive impairment) found significantly reduced alpha-band functional connectivity in patients with AF and cognitive impairment, and alpha-band wPLI was independently associated with cognitive impairment (OR = 0.44), supporting its potential as a biomarker.

papers.title: Neurophysiological and biological effects of music-based interventions in ADHD: a mini review.
papers.summary: This mini review synthesizes evidence on behavioral, neurophysiological, and biological effects of music-based interventions in ADHD. It reports potential effects on attention, impulse control, and emotional regulation, with neurophysiological findings indicating changes in auditory processing and cortical oscillations, but notes limited generalizability due to small samples and child-focused studies.

papers.title: Automated autism spectrum disorder detection using EEG signals and time-frequency visibility graphs.
papers.summary: This study proposes a dual-domain framework for automated EEG-based ASD classification using time-frequency analysis and Horizontal Visibility Graph-based network modeling. The DWT-HVG with a Soft Voting Ensemble achieved 93.54% accuracy and an AUC of 98.17% for ASD detection.

papers.title: White matter hyperintensity drives EEG microstate abnormalities in arteriosclerotic cerebral small vessel disease.
papers.summary: This study investigated EEG microstate abnormalities in arteriosclerotic cerebral small vessel disease and their association with white matter hyperintensity. It found reduced microstate C temporal parameters and altered transitions, with SVM/LR models achieving up to 76.67% accuracy for distinguishing WMHD from WMH-ND.

papers.title: Air and Bone-Conduction Masseteric Vestibular Evoked Myogenic Potentials: A Simulated Conductive Hearing Loss Study.
papers.summary: This study simulated conductive hearing loss in healthy young adults to compare air- and bone-conducted masseteric vestibular evoked myogenic potentials. It found that air-conducted responses were diminished or absent in simulated conductive loss, while bone-conducted responses remained robust, supporting their use in such pathologies.

papers.title: Negative BOLD response to interictal discharges in epilepsy using intracranial EEG-fMRI.
authors: the, Calgary Comprehensive Epilepsy Program collaborators
papers.summary: The study analyzed intracranial EEG-fMRI data from 57 epilepsy patients and found that positive BOLD responses were significantly closer to epileptogenic tissue than negative BOLD responses, while negative BOLD clusters showed greater overlap with the default mode network. These findings suggest prioritizing positive BOLD responses for presurgical localization.

papers.title: Developmental Regression and Seizures in a 28-Month-Old Child: A Delayed Diagnosis of Anti-N-Methyl-D-Aspartate Receptor Encephalitis.
papers.summary: The case report describes a 28-month-old child with anti-NMDA receptor encephalitis who presented with developmental regression and seizures but had normal MRI, CSF, and EEG initially. The diagnosis was delayed, but the patient responded to immunotherapy, highlighting the need to consider autoimmune encephalitis even with inconclusive initial tests.

papers.title: Adolescent depression recognition and symptom prediction based on multi-view EEG network: an exploratory study.
papers.summary: This exploratory study developed a Multi-view Adaptive Graph Convolutional Network (MVA-GCN) for adolescent depression recognition using resting-state EEG and compared it with questionnaire-based models. The MVA-GCN achieved 99.84% accuracy in the dataset, highlighting EEG network features as potential biomarkers, but findings require validation.

papers.title: Age-stratified interictal epileptiform discharges in SCN1A-related epilepsy: Association with early sodium channel-blocking antiseizure medication exposure.
papers.summary: This retrospective study of 57 SCN1A-related epilepsy patients found that interictal epileptiform discharges (IEDs) peak between 6-13 years and are strongly associated with prolonged early exposure to sodium channel-blocking antiseizure medications (≥11 months) in that age band (adjusted OR 28.74). The findings are exploratory and require confirmation.

papers.title: Enabling technologies for neural and biofluid interfaces: biocompatible materials with potential for neurodegenerative disease applications.
papers.summary: This review synthesizes advances in biocompatible materials for neural and biofluid interfaces, including soft elastomers, hydrogels, bioadhesives, and implantable platforms for brain, skin, and eye sensing. It assesses their potential for monitoring neurodegenerative diseases, highlighting challenges for geriatric populations and need for clinical validation.

papers.title: A Novel de Novo WAC Frameshift Variant in DeSanto-Shinawi Syndrome With Temporo-Occipital Epileptiform Activity and Congenital Cardiac Anomalies.
papers.journal: American journal of medical genetics. Part A
papers.summary: This case report describes a 9-year-old boy with DeSanto-Shinawi syndrome due to a novel de novo WAC frameshift variant (c.1793delT), presenting with developmental delay, epilepsy with temporo-occipital epileptiform activity, and congenital cardiac anomalies (ventricular septal defect, bicuspid aortic valve). It expands the clinical and mutational spectrum of DESSH.

papers.title: Neuroimaging in Addiction: Principles of Functional Near-infrared Spectroscopy and Its Emerging Role in De-addiction: A Narrative Review.
papers.summary: This narrative review examines the principles and applications of functional near-infrared spectroscopy (fNIRS) in addiction research and de-addiction therapy. It reports that fNIRS reliably detects altered prefrontal cortex hemodynamic responses during cue-reactivity and cognitive tasks, and that emerging applications include neurofeedback and machine-learning-based classification, suggesting its potential as a biomarker and monitoring tool.

papers.title: The First Iranian Patient with West Syndrome Due to a RYR3 Gene Variant: A Case Report and Literature Review.
papers.summary: This case report describes a novel de novo heterozygous variant in the RYR3 gene (c.4112T>C, p.Leu1371Pro) identified via trio-based whole-exome sequencing in an Iranian patient with West syndrome, supporting the potential pathogenic role of RYR3 in early-onset epileptic encephalopathy.

papers.title: Functional/dissociative seizures in a single women's rehabilitation center in Addis Ababa, Ethiopia: a single-center case series and thematic analysis of neuropsychiatric presentation, cultural meaning, and structural barriers to care.
papers.summary: This case series from Ethiopia describes six young women with clinically suspected functional/dissociative seizures, identifying themes of trauma, attachment disruption, dissociation, and cultural/systemic barriers to care, and highlighting the need for culturally adapted screening and trauma-informed assessment in settings without video-EEG.

papers.title: Physical activity and the Neuro-Immuno-Fascial interface in cancer patients: mechanisms, clinical evidence, and therapeutic integration.
papers.summary: This narrative review proposes the Neuro-Immuno-Fascial interface as a conceptual framework for how exercise may influence tumor biology, citing evidence of reduced recurrence and mortality in cancer patients, and outlining potential mechanisms such as mechanotransduction and autonomic rebalancing, while emphasizing that direct human evidence is lacking.

topic.label: EEG & Signal Methods
topic.description: EEG signal processing, sleep staging, neural time series, modeling, and practical analysis methods.
